rationale: The buyer is well-defined — Salesforce developers and architects at companies running custom Apex, who already pay enterprise Salesforce licenses and routinely spend on consultant engagements for exactly this kind of breaking-change audit. Pain severity is high: a misunderstood security mode change in production Apex triggers can expose data or break automations, and the Summer '26 API v67 change creates an immediate, time-bounded reason to buy. Buildability is plausible (Claude can read Apex code and cross-reference the v67 changelog), but operational autonomy sits at the gate floor — complex org configurations may surface edge cases requiring human review. Validate by offering a free audit to 10 orgs to confirm Claude can reliably handle real-world Apex trigger code.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an Apex API v67 security-mode audit: a Salesforce developer pastes their trigger code into an intake form, and Claude analyzes it against the Summer '26 system-mode vs. user-mode change, returning a flagged report of affected triggers with plain-English risk descriptions and recommended fixes. Build: the factory creates a Claude prompt loaded with the v67 release notes + Apex security model docs, connects it to a simple form and Stripe ($99–$299 per org audit, or $49/month for ongoing monitoring), and emails the report automatically. Sell: the factory drafts outreach to Salesforce developers identifiable on Stack Exchange (the question itself has answerers and commenters) and via LinkedIn searches for 'Salesforce developer API v67' — Youval approves each batch. Maintain: intake, analysis, and report delivery are fully automated; Youval's only touch is approving outreach and spot-checking flagged high-severity reports before they send. Time-sensitivity of the v67 window makes early validation critical.
notes: Hits min_total_to_build at exactly 6.5 but responsiveness is untested and the offer is time-sensitive to the Summer '26 release cycle. Keeping at validate until a reply signal is confirmed. All build gates met at their floors.
